t: A Greek successor state of Byzantium founded in 1204 on the south-eastern Black Sea coast by the Grand Komnenoi.
Its wealth came from trade between Persia and the Black Sea, carried by Genoese and Venetian merchants.
It survived by tribute and marriage alliances until Mehmed II took Trebizond in 1461, eight years after Constantinople fell.
dyk: Theodora of Trebizond, daughter of John IV, married the Turkmen ruler Uzun Hasan; their daughter was the mother of Shah Ismail I, founder of the Safavid dynasty of Persia.
ev: Alexios and David Komnenos seize Trebizond with Georgian troops
The Seljuks take Sinop and capture Alexios I
Trebizond becomes a vassal of the Mongols
John II gives up the title of Emperor of the Romans
Civil war between aristocratic factions weakens the empire
Alexios III begins a long reign that restores order
Emperor David surrenders Trebizond to Mehmed II
David and most of his family are executed in Constantinople
